additive_descent.consequence: no nontrivial additive Galois averaging is target-forced by the chosen-prime gate
additive_descent.reason: complete splitting identifies O_K/p with a product of F_p coordinates; vanishing of one coordinate does not force an orbit sum to vanish
additive_descent.theorem: for every nontrivial subgroup H, Tr_(K/K^H)(P) is not contained in P intersect K^H; the same failure holds for nontrivial additive character/idempotent projections

multiplicative_descent.consequence: passing through any subfield does not improve the black-box absolute norm bound (21 sqrt(p))^phi(p-1)
multiplicative_descent.false_positives: the norm can be divisible by p because a different split-prime coordinate vanishes even when the selected target is nonzero
multiplicative_descent.height_identity: if d=[K:Q], h=|H|, and every conjugate of T is at most B, each relative-norm conjugate is at most B^h and its absolute norm bound is B^(h*d/h)=B^d
multiplicative_descent.theorem: N_(K/K^H)(T) lies in P intersect K^H whenever T lies in P

setup.chosen_prime: the Teichmueller embedding fixes one prime P above p, and the selected gate is T in P
setup.splitting: p is unramified and p=1 mod (p-1), hence splits completely in K_p

stabilizer_dichotomy.bounded_degree_requirement: a degree-D descent requires a stabilizer of size at least phi(p-1)/D
stabilizer_dichotomy.finite_witness: both preselected selected-carrier zeros p=13 and p=47 have trivial stabilizer; this is exact finite evidence against automatic descent, not a density theorem
stabilizer_dichotomy.not_forced: chosen-prime membership alone imposes no equality between Galois coordinates and therefore forces no nontrivial stabilizer
